docs.title: systemspec-pricingpackaging
docs.text:
A Go-first, machine-readable description of a product's pricing and packaging. A Spec holds the tiers of a product's ladder, the plans in them with their prices, the features and limits each plan sets, one-time products, a marketplace fee, and the application access each tier grants. A pricing page, a limit check, a payment provider's prices and an account's entitlements are computed from it.

  • Concepts: tiers, plans, features, limits and grants.
  • Writing a spec: the document, with a complete example.
  • Using a spec: loading, checking features and limits, rendering a pricing page, and seeing what changed.
  • The normative description is SPEC.md.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
A product's offer is described once, as data, and everything else is computed from it.

Term Meaning Tier A position on the product's ladder, with a rank. "Free", "Plus", "Business". An account's entitlement carries its tier. Plan What an account can be on. A plan belongs to one tier, may have monthly and yearly prices, and sets features and limits. Free and arranged plans have no price. Feature Something a plan switches on, or sets to a level. A switch is on or off; a ladder has ordered levels such as community, email, priority. Limit Something a plan caps: a count, optionally per day or month. It can be unlimited, or fair use. Product A one-time purchase: a fixed price, or a price the seller sets with a floor. Marketplace The platform's share of sales by sellers, in basis points, optionally overridden per plan. Grant What a tier gives an account: access to an application, with a number of members or no limit. Default plan The free plan an unrecognised plan value resolves to, and the plan for an account when billing is not configured.

docs.title: Access is a grant, allowances are looked up
docs.text:
Two different things follow from an account's plan:

  • Access. Which applications the account may open and how many members it may have. This is the tier's grant, and it travels with the account's entitlement.
  • Allowances. Which features are on, at what level, and how many boards, items or runs. These are not copied into the entitlement. The host stores the account's plan and asks the Spec at the moment of a check.

So a price or an allowance can change without reissuing anything, and two plans in one tier can differ in allowances while giving the same access.

docs.title: Safe by construction
docs.text:
• An unknown plan is the default plan.
  • An unset feature is off, and an unset limit is zero.
  • "Unlimited" is its own field and never a zero or a missing value.
  • The default plan must be free, and its tier must grant something.
  • A Spec that breaks a rule is rejected with every error at once, each with a stable code (E001 to E013). Warnings (W001 to W006) are for review.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text: It is not a billing system: charging, subscriptions and webhooks are a runtime library's work, which reads a Spec. It does not decide who may buy or what a purchase issues; those stay with the product. It does not recommend prices.

docs.title: Using a spec
docs.text: Load the Spec once at startup and keep it. Every function below takes the account's plan ID, which your product stores with the account's subscription. An unknown ID is treated as the default plan.

docs.title: Features and levels
docs.text:
spec.Has(account.Plan, "audit_log")                // a switch, or a ladder at any level
spec.AtLeast(account.Plan, "support", "email")     // a ladder at or above a level
spec.Level(account.Plan, "support")                // "community", "email", ...

AtLeast is false for an unset ladder, a switch, an unknown feature or an unknown level, so a check can only grant what the Spec states.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
switch spec.Check(account.Plan, "boards", boardCount+1) { // usage after the action
case pricingspec.Allowed:
    // proceed
case pricingspec.Warn:
    // a fair-use allowance is exceeded: proceed, and flag the account
case pricingspec.Refuse:
    // tell the person which plan allows more
}

Check takes the usage after the action: with a maximum of 3 and 2 boards in use, adding a third is checked as 3 and is allowed. You count the usage, including per-month counts; the Spec defines the allowance. Allowance returns the maximum and the unlimited and fair-use flags, for showing "2 of 3 used".

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
for _, g := range spec.GrantsFor(account.Plan) {
    // g.Application, g.Seats, g.UnlimitedSeats
}

Use the grants when you turn a subscription into the account's entitlement. Do not copy features or limits into it.

docs.title: A pricing page
docs.text:
view := spec.PricingView()
for _, p := range view.Plans { /* a column: name, tier, prices, free, default */ }
for _, row := range view.Features { /* one row; row.Cells line up with view.Plans */ }
for _, row := range view.Limits { /* the same, with Max, Unlimited, FairUse */ }

The view is data, not text: you choose the words. Plans come in tier order, and the cells of every row are in the same order as the columns.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
for _, c := range pricingspec.Diff(oldSpec, newSpec) {
    fmt.Println(c) // changed plan plus: month price 1200 to 1500 [affects existing customers]
}

Run it on a pull request to see an offer change as a review. A change is marked as affecting existing customers when it makes things worse for accounts already on it: a higher price, a lower allowance, a removed feature or grant, or a removed plan.

docs.title: The tier and the entitlement
docs.text: An account's entitlement carries the plan's tier ID unchanged, and the tier's grants give it access. The account's plan, which you store, is what you pass to every function above. See the specification for the full mapping.

docs.title: Writing a spec
docs.text: A Spec is a JSON document. It is read with unknown fields rejected, so a typo is an error, not silently ignored. Its JSON Schema is schema/pricing.schema.json, for editors.

docs.title: A small offer
docs.text:
{
  "formatVersion": "1",
  "app": "taskboard",
  "currency": "usd",
  "defaultPlan": "free",
  "applications": [ { "id": "boards", "name": "Boards" } ],
  "tiers": [
    { "id": "free", "name": "Free", "rank": 1 },
    { "id": "plus", "name": "Plus", "rank": 2 }
  ],
  "features": [
    { "id": "support", "name": "Support", "levels": ["community", "email"] }
  ],
  "limits": [
    { "id": "boards", "name": "Boards", "unit": "board", "period": "none" }
  ],
  "plans": [
    {
      "id": "free", "name": "Free", "tier": "free", "selfServe": true,
      "features": [ { "feature": "support", "level": "community" } ],
      "limits": [ { "limit": "boards", "max": 3 } ]
    },
    {
      "id": "plus", "name": "Plus", "tier": "plus", "selfServe": true, "trialDays": 14,
      "prices": [
        { "interval": "month", "amountCents": 1200 },
        { "interval": "year", "amountCents": 12000 }
      ],
      "features": [ { "feature": "support", "level": "email" } ],
      "limits": [ { "limit": "boards", "max": 25 } ]
    }
  ],
  "entitlements": [
    { "tier": "free", "application": "boards", "seats": 3 },
    { "tier": "plus", "application": "boards", "seats": 10 }
  ]
}

Fuller offers are in examples/: a subscription tool with levelled features and fair-use allowances, and a marketplace with seller-set prices and per-plan fees.

docs.title: Rules worth knowing
docs.text:
• Amounts are integers in the currency's minor units: 1200 is $12.00.
  • Zero means zero. A limit a plan does not set, or sets to 0, allows nothing. Write "unlimited": true for no limit.
  • Ladders are only for levels that include the one below. A set of independent options (video from one provider, from another) is separate switches, not levels.
  • Fair use. With a max, exceeding it warns and flags the account for review instead of refusing. With unlimited, it records that the allowance is advertised as unlimited and subject to your fair-use policy.
  • The default plan is free and self-serve, and its tier needs a grant, so an account that is not billed can still open something.
  • Every other self-serve plan has a price. An arranged plan (selfServe false) may have none.
  • Seats live only in grants. To limit members, change the tier's grant.
  • A marketplace fee is in basis points (1000 is 10%), and a plan's platformFeeBps overrides it for sellers on that plan.

docs.title: Checking it
docs.text:
f, _ := os.Open("pricing.json")
spec, err := pricingspec.Load(f)
if err != nil {
    var ve *pricingspec.ValidationError
    if errors.As(err, &ve) {
        for _, is := range ve.Issues {
            fmt.Println(is) // E006 error: plans[1].features[0].level: ...
        }
    }
    return err
}
for _, w := range spec.Lint() {
    fmt.Println(w) // W002 warning: ...
}

Run it in CI so an invalid offer cannot ship. Lint warnings are for a person to look at; they never reject a Spec.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
Release notes, one file per version, newest first. The changelog is generated from CHANGELOG.json and lists every change with its commit.

The latest release, v0.1.0, is the first: a machine-readable description of a product's pricing and packaging, with validation, helpers for features and limits, a pricing view, an entitlement map and a diff.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, this project adheres to Semantic Versioning, commits follow Conventional Commits, and this changelog is generated by Structured Changelog.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• A Go-first, machine-readable description of a product's pricing and packaging: tiers, plans with prices, features (switches and ordered levels), limits (with periods and fair use), one-time products, a marketplace fee, and the application access each tier grants
  • Safe by construction: an unknown plan is the default plan, an unset feature is off, an unset limit is zero, and unlimited is its own field
  • Validation with stable error codes (E001 to E013) that reports every error at once, and lint warnings (W001 to W006) for review
  • Projections computed from the spec: a pricing view, a tier-to-entitlement map, and a diff that marks what affects existing customers

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• pricingspec types: Spec, Tier, Feature, Limit, Plan, Price, FeatureValue, LimitValue, Product, Marketplace and TierGrant, following the static-type profile with no schema composition (6a57f7b)
  • schema/pricing.schema.json generated from the Go types and embedded, with a test that fails when it is out of date (976d42f)
  • Load and Parse decode strictly, reject unknown fields and unknown format versions, and return a *ValidationError listing every error rule broken (E001 to E013) with a path (1bb1795)
  • Spec.Lint reports the review warnings W001 to W006: unlimited defaults without fair use, a higher tier priced under a lower one, unused features and limits, tiers without grants, level names that read as options, and annual prices that are no saving (811bdb2)
  • Helpers PlanOrDefault, Has, Level, AtLeast, Allowance, Check (allowed, warn or refuse), GrantsFor and TierRank; an unknown identifier never grants more (deae5dc)
  • PricingView orders plans by tier and lines features and limits up across them as data for a page; EntitlementMap lists each tier's grants in rank order (8f39a8e)
  • Diff compares two specs in a stable order and marks price increases, lowered allowances, removed features, lowered levels, removed grants, higher fees and removed plans as affecting existing customers (8ceb1d5)
  • Examples of a subscription tool and a marketplace, both invented, kept valid and free of warnings by tests (7d78714)

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• SPEC.md is the normative description of the model, the rule codes, resolution, projections and the mapping from a tier to account entitlements (0b1d170)
  • The fit of the model to three product shapes is recorded, with the changes it required (4201e64)
  • A user guide covers concepts, writing a spec and using a spec, built as an MkDocs site (07ae1ae)

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: • A test for every error and warning code, the loader's rejections, the helpers, golden files for the projections and the diff, and schema validation of the examples (da640d5)

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text: • Module, license, lint configuration and CI workflows (ea05786)

docs.title: v0.1.0
docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-22

The first release: a Go-first, machine-readable description of a product's pricing and packaging. A Spec holds the tiers of a product's ladder, the plans in them with their prices, the features and limits each plan sets, one-time products, a marketplace fee, and the application access each tier grants. A pricing page, a limit check, a payment provider's prices and an account's entitlements are computed from it, so none of them is maintained beside it.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One description of an offer. Tiers with an order; plans with monthly and yearly prices, trials, and free or arranged variants; features that are a switch or an ordered ladder of levels; limits with an optional period and a fair-use flag; fixed and seller-set one-time products; a marketplace fee with per-plan overrides. See Concepts.
  • Safe by construction. An unknown plan is the default plan, an unset feature is off, an unset limit is zero, and "unlimited" is its own field and never a zero or a missing value. The default plan must be free and its tier must grant something.
  • Validated with stable codes. A Spec that breaks an error rule (E001 to E013) is rejected with every error at once, each with a path. Lint warnings (W001 to W006) are for review and never reject.
  • Access is a grant; allowances are looked up. What an account may open and how many members it may have is its tier's grant and travels with its entitlement. Features and limits stay in the Spec and are read by the account's plan at the moment of a check.
  • Projections, not copies. A pricing view for a page to render, an entitlement map from tier to grants, and a diff between two Specs that marks what affects existing customers.
  • A generated JSON Schema from the Go types, linted with the family's schema tool with no findings.

docs.title: What is in it
docs.text:
Part Contents SPEC.md The normative description of the model, the validation and lint rules, resolution, and the mapping from a tier to account entitlements pricingspec The types, Load and Parse, Validate and Lint, the plan, feature and limit helpers, PricingView, EntitlementMap and Diff schema pricing.schema.json, generated and embedded examples/ A subscription tool and a marketplace, both invented docs/ A user guide: concepts, writing a spec, using a spec 
spec, err := pricingspec.Load(f)            // strict decode, then validate
spec.Has(account.Plan, "audit_log")
spec.AtLeast(account.Plan, "support", "email")
spec.Check(account.Plan, "boards", boards+1) // Allowed, Warn or Refuse
view := spec.PricingView()
changes := pricingspec.Diff(oldSpec, newSpec)

docs.title: Rules the model enforces
docs.text:
• Amounts are integers in the currency's minor units, at most one price per interval.
  • A ladder's levels are ordered and distinct; levels are for ladders where each level includes the one below, and a set of independent options is several switches.
  • A limit is a number or explicitly unlimited. With a number, fair use makes exceeding it warn and flag the account for review; with unlimited, it records that the allowance is subject to the host's fair-use policy.
  • Seats live only in a tier's grants.
  • Every plan names a declared tier, every value a declared feature or limit, and every grant a declared tier and application.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go get github.com/plexusone/systemspec-pricingpackaging@v0.1.0

Requires Go 1.26. The package imports the standard library only; the schema generator and the tests use invopop/jsonschema and santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema.

docs.title: Upgrade notes
docs.text: None: this is the first release. formatVersion is "1"; a reader rejects any other version.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• One currency per Spec. Prices in several currencies are not expressible.
  • No seat-based or metered prices, coupons, regional pricing or tax. A plan has a flat price per interval.
  • What a purchase issues, who may pay, and what payment may never buy are not in the model. They are policy that stays with the product that uses the Spec.
  • Usage is the host's. The Spec defines an allowance and the check; the host counts usage, including per day or month.
  • No command-line tool. Validation, lint, the pricing view and the diff are library functions.
  • Proven on invented offers and one draft of a real one. The model was checked against three product shapes and its examples, and a billing library that consumes it is being built; a production trial has not happened yet. The format may change before a 1.0 if that trial finds a gap.
  • Format version 1 is a promise only for additive changes: new optional fields do not bump it.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Module Use github.com/invopop/jsonschema Generating the schema from the types github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 Validating examples against the schema, in tests

docs.title: systemspec-pricingpackaging: Fit of the Model to Three Product Shapes
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-001 Work item: RMI-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-001

The model in the TRD was written from one product's plans. This record checks it against three invented shapes that between them cover what the first release must express, and lists what did not fit and how the model changes. The shapes are composites; none is a real product.

docs.title: The three shapes
docs.text:
A. A tools suite for small teams. Three applications behind one sign-in. Tiers Free, Starter, Team and an arranged Enterprise. Limits are counts (projects, records) and a daily rate; one feature is a ladder (sync: daily, hourly). Seats differ by tier. One platform account, several applications.

B. A publishing platform for sellers. Tiers Basic, Plus, Pro. Many differences are levels, not switches: branding (required, optional, removed), report and analytics depth, export styling, API access (none, limited, full). Item count is a limit, "viewers" is advertised as unlimited with a fair-use policy, and exports per month is a fair-use allowance. Sellers sell items to buyers and the platform takes a fee; selling is unavailable on Basic. Media hosting differs by tier as a set of providers.

C. A household app. A free tier that nobody pays for, a household subscription paid by one adult, a one-time purchase that issues a verified record, a marketplace where sellers set prices and the platform takes a share, and an arranged institution licence. Rules say what payment may never buy.

docs.title: What fit
docs.text: Need In the model Free, monthly and yearly plans; arranged plans Plan with Prices, SelfServe Counts with explicit unlimited LimitValue with Unlimited A daily or monthly allowance Limit.Period A ladder of levels (sync, branding, report and analytics depth, export style, API access) Feature.Levels, ordered; unset is off A switch (custom domain, selling, team management) A feature without levels A trial Plan.TrialDays A one-time purchase with a fixed price Product A seller-set price with a floor Product.SellerSet, MinAmountCents A marketplace share Marketplace.PlatformFeeBps Several applications behind one account Grants per tier and application Seats differing by tier TierGrant.Seats or UnlimitedSeats

docs.title: What did not fit, and the change
docs.text:
1. The marketplace fee can differ by plan. In shape B a seller on a higher plan may pay a lower share. A single Marketplace.PlatformFeeBps cannot say that. Change: Plan.PlatformFeeBps is an optional override of the marketplace default.
  2. Advertised "unlimited" with a fair-use policy. In B, viewers are unlimited but subject to anti-abuse limits. Unlimited and a numeric fair-use threshold are different things. Change: LimitValue.FairUse may accompany Unlimited; then it means "advertised as unlimited, subject to the host's fair-use policy", and Max is ignored. With a Max, FairUse means crossing it warns and flags rather than refuses.
  3. A set of providers is not a ladder. B's media hosting is "one provider", then "that one or an external one", then "external or integrated". Where the sets are nested this is a ladder, but it need not be. Change: the rule is that levels are only for monotonic ladders; a capability that is a set (media providers, payment methods) is several features without levels. A lint warns when a levelled feature's levels read as names of independent options.
  4. Applications were an undeclared string. A grant named an application with nothing to check it against. Change: the document declares Applications, and grants refer to them. This closes the open question in the TRD.
  5. Seats had two homes. A plan limit and a tier grant could both say how many members. Change: seats are in grants only. A product that wants a member cap as a limit expresses it as a grant; there is one place to enforce it.
  6. A one-time product that issues something. In C a purchase issues a verified record. The model records a price, not what the purchase gives. Decision: what a product grants is the host's, identified by the product ID it receives when the purchase completes. The spec stays a description of the offer, not of fulfilment. Recorded as out of scope for the first release.
  7. Who may pay, and what payment may never buy. C's rules (one adult pays, payment never buys an advantage) are policy. Decision: policy stays with the host. A feature may carry an advisory Category in a later release so a lint can flag a paid-only feature in a category the product has promised to keep free; it is not in the first release.
  8. Audience. Pricing pages group plans for individuals, families, teams and institutions. Decision: deferred; a page can group by tier.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Two additions to the types (Plan.PlatformFeeBps, Applications), one change of meaning (FairUse with Unlimited), and two rules (levels only for ladders; seats only in grants). Three things are recorded as out of scope for the first release: what a product grants, payer policy, and audience. The model otherwise holds for all three shapes without extension.

docs.title: systemspec-pricingpackaging: Plan
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemspec-pricingpackaging

Implements the PRD and TRD. The roadmap holds the work items and their status.

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
• Small first. The first release covers recurring plans, one-time products, a marketplace fee and the tier-to-entitlement map, and no more. Offers that need more extend the model with examples behind them.
  • Types, then schema, then rules. The Go types are specified and frozen, the schema generated from them, and validation and lint written against the types.
  • Two shapes before freezing. A subscription product with levelled features and a marketplace product both have to be expressible, so the model is not frozen against one.
  • Projections are tested against golden files, so a change to a page, a map or a diff is visible in review.
  • Public-ready from the first commit. Examples are invented; no real products, prices or customers.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text: Phase Theme Outcome 1 Design The model checked against two product shapes, the tier and entitlement vocabulary fixed, and the TRD frozen 2 The model The types, the generated schema, validation and lint 3 Helpers and projections Plan, feature and limit helpers; the pricing view, entitlement map and diff 4 Examples and release Invented examples for two shapes, a guide, and v0.1.0

docs.title: Order and dependencies
docs.text: Phase 1 gates the rest. Phase 3 depends on the types from Phase 2. The billing library that consumes the spec is planned in its own repository and starts once the types are frozen.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Validation and lint: a test for each rule.
  • Helpers: unknown identifiers, level ordering, unlimited versus zero.
  • Projections: golden files.
  • Schema: generated, linted with the family's tool, and used to validate the examples.
  • A billing library imports the package and builds a pricing view, a limit check and a provider plan from an example before v0.1.0.

docs.title: systemspec-pricingpackaging: Product Requirements
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemspec-pricingpackaging

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
A product's pricing and packaging (what each tier costs, what it includes, what it limits, and what access it gives an account) is decided by people and then scattered into code: a price in a payment dashboard, a feature check in a handler, a tier name in a database column, a table on a marketing page. The copies drift. A change to a price or a limit is an edit in several places, no one can review the whole offer as one thing, and nothing can tell whether the pages, the checks and the payment provider agree.

Other aspects of a system already have a machine-readable description in this family of specs: how an API is styled, what cryptography is used, how it is deployed. Pricing and packaging has none.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. One description of a product's pricing and packaging, as data: tiers, plans, prices, features (on, off or a level), limits (with periods and fair-use), one-time products and marketplace fees.
  2. A mapping from tier to account entitlements: which applications and how many seats a tier grants, so a paid plan can become what an account may use, using a shared vocabulary of tiers.
  3. Safe by construction. Unknown plans resolve to a declared free default; "unlimited" is explicit and never a zero; a spec that would grant more than it states is rejected.
  4. Validated and reviewable. A schema, lint rules for common mistakes, and a diff that shows what changed in an offer.
  5. Projections, not copies. A pricing-page view, an entitlement map and a description of what a payment provider should hold are computed from the spec, never maintained alongside it.
  6. Product-neutral and minimal. Any product can describe its offer; the first release covers recurring plans, one-time products and a marketplace fee, and nothing more.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Not a billing system. Charging, subscriptions, webhooks and payouts are a runtime library's work. This is the description it reads.
  • Not a pricing policy. The spec records decisions; it does not recommend prices.
  • Not revenue reporting, tax, invoicing or accounting.
  • Not a user interface. It supplies the data a pricing page renders.
  • Not a licence manager for installed software.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
• Product owners, who write and review a product's offer as one document.
  • Billing libraries and platforms, which read it to create prices, check features and limits, and turn a subscription into entitlements.
  • Front ends, which render a pricing page from the spec's view.
  • Reviewers and agents, who diff offers and lint them.

docs.title: Functional
docs.text:
• A Spec document with a format version, a product identifier, a currency, declared tiers with an order, declared features (each on/off or with ordered levels), declared limits (each with a unit and optionally a period), plans and one-time products, an optional marketplace fee, a default plan, and the entitlements each tier grants.
  • Validation: unique identifiers, declared references, one tier per plan, integer prices, explicit unlimited, a free default, and ordered levels.
  • Helpers: resolve a plan or the default, test a feature or a level, and check a count against a limit with allowed, warn and refuse results.
  • Projections: a pricing view for rendering, a tier-to-entitlement map, and a diff between two specs.
  • A generated JSON Schema that passes the family's lint with no findings.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• Go-first. The Go types are the source of truth; the schema is generated.
  • Static types. Following the family's profile: no schema composition, no untyped or heterogeneous maps; vocabularies are enums and optional data is named fields.
  • No payment or framework dependency. The package imports the standard library only.
  • Public-ready. Examples are invented; no real products, prices or customers appear in the repository.

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text:
• A product's offer is one reviewable file, and a pricing page, a limit check and a provider plan are all computed from it.
  • A price or limit change is a diff of that file.
  • Two products with different shapes (a subscription tool and a marketplace) are both expressed without extending the model.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Over-modeling. Offers vary widely. The first release is held to recurring plans, one-time products and a marketplace fee, and grows by examples.
  • Static-type constraints make "a feature is either on or a level" awkward; the model uses explicit named fields for each.
  • Tier vocabulary disagreement between products. The spec makes tiers declared and ordered per product and defines the mapping to entitlements, so differences are explicit.

docs.title: ROADMAP — systemspec-pricingpackaging: Pricing and Packaging Spec
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemspec-pricingpackaging

Specs: PRD, TRD, PLAN. Work items carry stable IDs (RMI-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-NNN), are reviewed and executed by phase, and commits implementing one carry the trailer Refs: RMI-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-<NNN>.

Later, not scheduled: prices in several currencies, seat-based and metered prices, coupons, regional pricing, and a command-line tool.

docs.text:

  • [x] RMI-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-001 Check the proposed model against two product shapes (a subscription tool with levelled features, and a marketplace with one-time sales) and record what does not fit

docs.title: systemspec-pricingpackaging: Technical Requirements
docs.text:
Initiative: INIT-SYSTEMSPECPRICINGPACKAGING-001 Repository: github.com/plexusone/systemspec-pricingpackaging

Status: frozen for v0.1 by Phase 1. The normative description is SPEC.md; this document records the reasoning. The model was checked against three product shapes in FIT.md, which changed it as listed under Changes from the fit check.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• The Spec is the source of truth. Everything else (a page, a check, a provider plan) is a projection.
  • Static types. No oneOf, anyOf or allOf, no untyped or heterogeneous maps. A feature value is an explicit pair of named fields, not a value that is sometimes a boolean and sometimes a string.
  • Facts, not prose. Descriptions are display text; rules are fields.
  • Safe defaults. Nothing grants more than the spec states.
  • Standard library only.

Package: pricingspec. Generated schema: schema/pricing.schema.json, linted with schemakit lint --property-case camelCase.

docs.title: The model (proposed)
docs.text:
type Spec struct {
    FormatVersion string
    App           string        // identifies the product; tags what a provider holds
    Currency      string        // ISO code, lowercase
    DefaultPlan   string        // a plan ID; the free plan
    Applications  []Application // what grants may refer to
    Tiers         []Tier
    Features      []Feature
    Limits        []Limit
    Plans         []Plan
    Products      []Product     // one-time purchases
    Marketplace   *Marketplace
    Entitlements  []TierGrant   // what each tier grants an account
}

docs.title: Tiers
docs.text:
type Tier struct {
    ID   string  // "free", "plus", "pro"
    Name string
    Rank int     // order, lowest first; unique
}

A tier is a position in the product's ladder, and the word the entitlement and the subscription use. A plan belongs to exactly one tier. A tier may have several plans (monthly and yearly are prices on one plan; a separate plan is for a different offer at the same tier).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
type Feature struct {
    ID          string
    Name        string
    Description string
    Levels      []string  // empty: the feature is on or off; else ordered, lowest first
}

type FeatureValue struct {
    Feature string
    Enabled bool      // for a feature without levels
    Level   string    // for a feature with levels; one of its Levels
}

A plan lists a FeatureValue for each feature it sets; an unset feature is off (or at no level). A check asks Has(feature) for on/off features or AtLeast(feature, level) for levelled ones.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
type Limit struct {
    ID          string
    Name        string
    Unit        string   // "board", "seat", "export"
    Period      Period   // none, day, month
    Description string
}

type LimitValue struct {
    Limit     string
    Unlimited bool     // explicit; Max must be zero when true
    Max       int      // zero means zero
    FairUse   bool     // with Max: crossing warns instead of refusing; with Unlimited: advertised as unlimited, subject to the host's policy
}

Unlimited is a boolean, not a null or a zero, so a mistake never grants more than intended. The host counts usage (including per period); the spec defines the allowance and the check.

docs.title: Plans and products
docs.text:
type Plan struct {
    ID        string
    Name      string
    Tier      string
    SelfServe bool         // can be bought through checkout; false: arranged
    PlatformFeeBps *int    // optional override of the marketplace fee
    TrialDays int
    Prices    []Price      // empty for a free or arranged plan
    Features  []FeatureValue
    Limits    []LimitValue
}

type Price struct {
    Interval    Interval   // month, year
    AmountCents int64
}

type Product struct {                 // a one-time purchase
    ID          string
    Name        string
    AmountCents int64      // fixed price, or zero when SellerSet
    SellerSet   bool       // the seller sets the price
    MinAmountCents int64   // floor for a seller-set price
}

type Marketplace struct {
    PlatformFeeBps int     // basis points, 0 to 10000
}

docs.title: Entitlements
docs.text:
type TierGrant struct {
    Tier        string
    Application string   // the application the tier grants access to
    Seats       int      // 0 with Unlimited false means none
    UnlimitedSeats bool
}

This is the tier-to-access map: what an account on a tier may use. A runtime that turns a subscription into an entitlement reads the plan's tier and then this list. Features and limits are not copied into entitlements; they are looked up in the Spec by plan at the moment of a check, so prices and allowances can change without reissuing anything.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Errors (the Spec is rejected):

  • Duplicate IDs among tiers, features, limits, plans or products.
  • A plan whose tier, or a value whose feature or limit, is not declared.
  • A level not among the feature's levels; a feature with levels given a boolean.
  • Duplicate or non-positive tier ranks.
  • A negative amount, an amount not in minor units, or two prices for one interval.
  • A default plan that is missing, not self-serve free (no price), or in no tier.
  • A Product that is seller-set with no minimum, or fixed with no amount.
  • A Marketplace fee outside 0 to 10000.

Lint warnings (reviewable, not fatal):

  • No free tier, or a free plan with unlimited limits and no fair-use note.
  • A paid plan with a lower-ranked tier than a cheaper plan.
  • A feature declared and never used; a limit declared and never used.
  • A tier with no entitlement grant.

docs.title: Helpers
docs.text:
spec.PlanOrDefault(id string) Plan
plan.Has(feature string) bool
plan.AtLeast(feature, level string) bool
plan.Check(limit string, after int) Decision // after: usage after the action; Allowed, Warn, Refuse
spec.TierRank(tier string) int

An unknown plan ID returns the default plan. Checks never panic and never grant on an unknown identifier.

docs.title: Projections
docs.text:
• PricingView: plans in tier order with prices by interval, and a feature and limit matrix with display names, for a page to render.
  • EntitlementMap: tier to its grants.
  • Diff: two Specs compared into added, removed and changed plans, prices, features, limits and grants, with price increases and removed grants marked as changes that affect existing customers.

A description of what a payment provider should hold (products and prices by a stable key) is computed from the Spec by the billing library that syncs it, not here.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: FormatVersion is a string, bumped on a change to the document format. New optional fields are additions. A reader rejects a version it does not know.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Table tests for every validation error and lint warning.
  • Round-trip: Go → JSON → Go, and the generated schema validates the examples.
  • Helper tests for unknown identifiers, level ordering, unlimited versus zero, and fair-use results.
  • Golden files for the projections and the diff.
  • The family's schema lint with zero findings.

docs.title: Changes from the fit check
docs.text:
FIT.md checked the draft against three product shapes. The model changed in these ways, all reflected in SPEC.md:

  • Plan.PlatformFeeBps overrides the marketplace fee per plan.
  • Applications are declared, and grants refer to them.
  • FairUse may accompany Unlimited.
  • Levels are only for monotonic ladders; a set of independent options is several switches.
  • Seats live only in grants.
  • What a one-time purchase issues, who may pay and audience grouping are out of scope for v0.1.

docs.title: Tier vocabulary and the mapping to entitlements
docs.text: Tiers are declared per product with an order; there is no global vocabulary, and ranks of different products are not comparable. An account's entitlement carries the plan's tier ID unchanged. Access (applications, seats, validity) is the tier's grant and travels with the entitlement. Features and limits are read from the plan the host stores with the subscription, so two plans in one tier can differ in allowances while giving the same access. The rules are in SPEC.md under Entitlement mapping.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Whether prices in several currencies belong in the first release.
  • How a product with more than one deployable (several applications) shares tiers.
